# `.github/workflows`

The workflows, which the root's Workflow describes as rules.

The rules across the game are the [root AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).

- `branch-policy.yml`: fails a PR whose branch holds a merge commit (PR branches are linear).
- `pr-preview-build.yml`: builds a PR's preview with a read-only token and no secrets (the lab's, the preview scripts' and the previews service's unit tests, the typecheck and build, the asset paths), forks included, for its folder on the previews service, `/pr-preview/pr-N/<sha7>/` (`--base`: the service serves each PR under `/pr-preview` at its origin's root, as Pages served them on last-stand.cc).
- **Dokci builds the previews too** ([`server/game-preview`](../../server/game-preview/AGENTS.md), at `https://pr-N.ls.wellscoped.dev/`, linked from the PR's "Dokci preview" check), without Actions; the two below run beside it until those are seen working, then go.
- `pr-preview.yml`: a `workflow_run`, always the copy on `main`, which checks the artifact's PR number against the API and sends the build to our own previews service ([`server/previews`](../../server/previews/AGENTS.md), on the relay's host, `PREVIEW_ORIGIN`). **Never run PR code in it.** It holds no code of its own: each step calls a module of [`scripts/preview`](../../scripts/preview/AGENTS.md), checked out from the run's own commit (main's head) and unit-tested (`npm run preview:test`). Its secret is the `pr-preview` environment's `PREVIEWS_TOKEN` (the owner's; the same value as Dokci's `LS_PREVIEWS_TOKEN`), which only jobs naming that environment get.
- **Why not Pages any more** (#352): each publish deployed the whole aggregated site (some 77 MB, uploaded in 3 s), then GitHub held the deployment `queued` for 102 to 330 s before deploying it in 5 (measured from the runs' logs on 2026-11-06), and once over 600 s (run 42265349531: cancelled, "publication failed"); Pages' CDN also served a path's old copy for up to 10 minutes, so each build needed a folder of its own and probe files to know it was served. The service serves a build the moment its upload answers.
- **Each build has a folder of its own**, `pr-preview/pr-N/<sha7>/`, which the comment links. `pr-preview/pr-N/` is the stable page (`.github/preview-index.html`, main's copy, sent with each publish), which goes to the newest build by the PR's `latest.json` (building, ready or failed), served beside it, never cached: while a push builds it says how long, the previous build linked as such (#292). The service keeps a PR's newest three folders and the one `latest.json` names; a pruned folder's page goes to the stable page, a gone PR's to the game.
- **Every publish catches up the others** (`pr-preview.yml`'s publish job): it publishes its own build and, for every open PR whose `latest.json` doesn't record its head as ready or failed, that head's newest finished build, its artifact downloaded (`gh run download`, plain files only) and its `pr.json` checked against the API as its own is; every preview kept of a PR no longer open is removed. A build is sent, read back at its public address, and only then does its PR's `latest.json` say `ready`, and only if the PR's head is still that commit (an older build's publish never overtakes a newer one's). Each PR's sticky comment is written by the job itself (the marker `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` uses), a checklist while it goes (`progressMessage`: built, sent, served), then what came of it with how long sending and serving took. It runs for every finished build, cancelled and skipped ones too, and after every production deploy (a merged PR's preview removed). There is no concurrency group: the service takes one change at a time, and two publishes of one build send the same files. A build a catch-up published is skipped when its own run comes (its run's URL is in `latest.json`). Run the workflow by hand (`gh workflow run pr-preview.yml`) to catch up without a build; `--ref` a branch runs that branch's copy, which is how a change to it is tried before it's merged.
- `deploy-pages.yml`: on a merge to `main`, production on `gh-pages`, alone (the previews' old `pr-preview/` folders went with the first deploy after they moved), the `pages-publisher` group holding one deploy at a time.

Don't switch Pages to "GitHub Actions only", and don't delete the `gh-pages` branch.
